## 1. The urban growth rings (1985–2015)

The cartographic monograph below documents the physical settlement rings of **Chengdu** across four historical development epochs:

- <span style="color: #c75c3d; font-weight: bold;">● Pre-1985 Core</span>: Historic urban core and initial post-1949 industrial settlements.
- <span style="color: #2e5a48; font-weight: bold;">● 1986–1995 Wave</span>: Early reform, opening up, and Deng Xiaoping's 1992 Southern Tour (*Nanxun*).
- <span style="color: #457b9d; font-weight: bold;">● 1996–2005 Wave</span>: WTO entry, export industrialization, and new development zones (*Kaifaqu*).
- <span style="color: #e9c46a; font-weight: bold;">● 2006–2015 Wave</span>: High-speed rail expansion, modern new cities (*Xinqu*), and peri-urban consolidation.

::: {.map-container}
!['The urban growth rings: Chengdu'](../output/maps/chengdu_hero.png)
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Rapid Transit & Municipal Metro Infrastructure"}
**Chengdu** operates an extensive urban rapid transit network comprising **17 operational metro lines** and **365 passenger stations** (source: AMap 高德地图 / Ministry of Transport of the PRC):

- **Key metro corridors**: `地铁1号线`, `地铁2号线`, `S3(资阳)线`, `地铁3号线`, `地铁4号线`, `地铁5号线`, `地铁6号线`, `地铁7号线`
- **Cartographic overlay**: Illustrated on the main poster above, connecting historical settlement cores with peripheral development zones.
- **Transit alignment**: High-frequency metro corridors provide multi-directional connectivity between the historical core (Pre-1985 settlement) and outer-ring state-level expansion zones (*Kaifaqu* and *Xinqu*).
:::

## 5. Five-year milestone chronology

| Milestone Year | Urban Footprint (km²) | Growth vs. 1985 Baseline | Share of 2015 Footprint |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **1985** | 208.06 km² | 1.00× (Baseline) | 13.3% |
| **1990** | 307 km² | 1.48× | 19.6% |
| **1995** | 479.44 km² | 2.3× | 30.7% |
| **2000** | 736.02 km² | 3.54× | 47.1% |
| **2005** | 969.14 km² | 4.66× | 62.0% |
| **2010** | 1269.07 km² | 6.1× | 81.1% |
| **2015** | 1564.15 km² | **7.52×** | 100.0% |

## 6. Archival cartography & wiki resources

Direct links to open knowledge, semantic geodata, and scanned map collections for **Chengdu**:

- 📖 **English Wikipedia**: [Chengdu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chengdu) — In-depth overview of history, urban development, demographic shifts, and regional governance.
- 🌐 **Chinese Wikipedia (中文维基百科)**: [成都市](https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E6%88%90%E9%83%BD%E5%B8%82) — Authoritative municipal boundaries, administrative subdivisions, and local transport infrastructure.
- 🏷️ **Wikidata Knowledge Base**: [Q30002 (Chengdu)](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q30002) — Semantic knowledge graph entity with geocoordinates, OpenStreetMap tags, and linked administrative entities.
- 🗺️ **Wikimedia Commons Map Repository**: [Category:Maps of Chengdu](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category%3AMaps%20of%20Chengdu) — Community-curated media repository containing thematic, administrative, and transport maps.
- 📜 **Historical maps collection**: [Category:Old maps of Chengdu](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category%3AOld%20maps%20of%20Chengdu) — Scanned historical maps, municipal plans, and early surveys.
- 🔍 **Scanned Maps & Historical Sheets Search**: [Explore scanned bitmap and topographic maps of Chengdu on Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?search=Chengdu+map&title=Special:MediaSearch&type=image)

- 🌐 **UCSB ArcGIS Online Web Map**: [View interactive Web Map (item 636bb82ea14944a5b719fc46cf055a53)](https://ucsb.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=636bb82ea14944a5b719fc46cf055a53#overview)

## 7. Sources & methodology attributions

The quantitative and spatial indicators for **Chengdu** are synthesized from the following primary sources:

1. **Urban Footprint & Built-Up Surface**: German Aerospace Center (DLR) [World Settlement Footprint Evolution (1985–2015)](https://download.geoservice.dlr.de/WSF_EVO/). 30m resolution multi-decadal satellite detection (*Marconcini et al., 2020, Nature Scientific Data*).
2. **Permanent Resident Population**: National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), [Seventh National Population Census (第七次全国人口普查 / 七普 2020)](http://www.stats.gov.cn/). Resident population: **20.94M** (National Rank: **#1** of 47).
3. **National Urban Tier Classification**: Esri / [ArcGIS Online Big Cities Points FeatureServer](https://services1.arcgis.com/4TXrdeWh0RyCqPgB/arcgis/rest/services/big_cities_points/FeatureServer), National City Rank: **N/A** of 184 major Chinese cities.
4. **UCSB Study Cities & Curated Layers**: University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB) [Urban Atlas post-AGSL Web Map](https://ucsb.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=636bb82ea14944a5b719fc46cf055a53#overview) & [study_cities FeatureServer](https://services1.arcgis.com/4TXrdeWh0RyCqPgB/arcgis/rest/services/study_cities/FeatureServer/0) (DianPing rank: #4, RU topos: `x`, ZH city atlas: `x`, Planet: `x`).
4. **National Railway & Municipal Transit**:
   - **National Passenger Rail Network**: China Railway (中国国家铁路集团 / 12306) and National Railway Administration of China (NRA), covering national high-speed corridors (PDL) and conventional trunk lines.
   - **Urban Subway Network**: AMap (高德地图) Subway Platform and PRC Ministry of Transport (MOT) Urban Rail Transit database (17 lines, 365 stations for Chengdu).
6. **Administrative Boundaries**: [GADM Database of Global Administrative Areas (v4.1)](https://gadm.org/), University of California, Davis.
7. **Archival Cartography & Historical Surveys**: American Geographical Society Library (AGSL) Map Collection & [Wikimedia Foundation](https://www.wikimedia.org/) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/), [Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/), and [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/)).
